subject: Day 47: mirror play minutes
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 47. Head control is steadying when he is held upright, and face-tracking is one of the strongest motivators available. A few minutes of mirror play doubles as motor practice and face-circuit calibration.

Action items
- Hold Avi upright in front of a baby-safe mirror for two to three minutes during an alert window; the face in the glass pulls his head up and steady, so head-control practice and visual engagement happen at once.
- Have infant acetaminophen on hand ahead of the 2-month vaccines; the pediatrician will give a weight-based dose, and dosing after the shots rather than before avoids blunting the antibody response.
- Confirm the daycare or nanny start date aligns with the return-to-work date, with a one-to-two-week buffer.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Hiccups during or after feeds and quiet startles at loud sounds.
- [monitor] Asymmetric movement or a persistent head turn to one side; document it and raise it at the 2-month visit.
- [monitor] Forceful arching during or after feeds with frequent painful spit-up, which can point to reflux; note the pattern for the pediatrician.
- [call within 24h] Persistent vomiting beyond 24 hours, or refusal of several feeds in a row.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C), lethargy disproportionate to activity, blue or grey color, or persistent grunting at rest. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Hold him at the mirror for two to three minutes and let the head-steadiness practice double as face-circuit calibration; self-recognition comes much later, but the visual tracking is building now. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Play the chosen instrument's Suzuki listening recording during quiet play; early repeated exposure builds the auditory template the Suzuki method relies on later. Suzuki Association: https://suzukiassociation.org/
- Take a carrier walk outside with his chin off his chest and face visible, giving him upright air, daylight, and varied motion input. AAP HealthyChildren on movement, birth to three months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 49: 2-month visit prep; build the question list.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit and first vaccines.
- Day 57-72: post-vaccine 24-48 hour fussiness window.
- Day 95-105: 100-day photo session window.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
